next_step_summary: The first real March-August 2025 text-layer contract run completed with gemini-3.6-flash on the first provider attempt in 35.334 seconds and returned a high-completeness structured audit. The run confirmed that the model can read major lease mechanisms but also exposed model-owned prioritization/remediation defects: security-cheque mechanics were underweighted versus amount/market comparisons, broad fundamental-breach wording was not fully reconciled with the contract's specific cure mechanics, AS-IS remained a warning despite related repair protections, the handover defect-remediation procedure was underemphasized, and the report invented generic missing clauses, market norms, and numeric rewrite proposals. PR #272 wires the existing deterministic Question Engine core inventories into the whole-contract prompt, requires cross-clause second-pass resolution, blocks unsupported market/numeric invention, and suppresses ungated model-owned rewrite advice, generic missing-clause wishlists, and market-comparison prose in the local persisted report. Provider route, privacy gate, OCR scope, dependencies and network destinations are unchanged. After PR #272 validation/merge, rerun the same reviewed contract once and compare specifically: complete 20,000 NIS security-cheque mechanism questions; broad breach versus the existing 7-day rent cure; AS-IS versus repair allocation; the 21-day inspection/10-day correction return procedure; absence of generic option/insurance missing warnings; and absence of invented 2-3 month, 14-day, 48-hour, or 2,000-3,000 NIS recommendations.
